macros.name: ArrayRecord
macros.doc: Individual records of the original file, from the most recent \readdef, may be recalled with the \ArrayRecord macro.

macros.name: arraytomacro
macros.doc: The command takes the array name and index as the initial arguments followed by a generic macro name into which to place the unexpanded tokens of the indexed array cell.

macros.name: initarray
macros.doc: Arrays can be initialized with the \initarray command, rather than being read from a file.

macros.name: mergearray
macros.doc: The contents of one array can be merged into another by way of the \mergearray command.

macros.name: ncols
macros.doc: The macros \nrows and \ncols, which were gleaned from the file structure, may be used in the subsequent \readarray invocation to specify the array dimensions.

macros.name: nocheckbounds
macros.doc: The setting \nocheckbounds is used when bounds are not to be checked.

macros.name: nrows
macros.doc: The macros \nrows and \ncols, which were gleaned from the file structure, may be used in the subsequent \readarray invocation to specify the array dimensions.

macros.name: readarray
macros.doc: The \readarray command, used to convert raw parsable data into data arrays, takes three arguments.

macros.name: readarrayendlinechar
macros.doc: To recover the LaTeX way of treating end-of-lines, the count \readarrayendlinechar is provided, which can be set in the manner desired for subsequent invocations of \readdef.

macros.name: readarraysepchar
macros.doc: The default separator is a space character but the separator may be specified by way of \readarraysepchar{separator}.

macros.name: readrecordarray
macros.doc: The command \readrecordarray can be used to stick the individual “file records” from a designated file into a 1-D array. The \readrecordarray command takes two arguments: a file name containing data records, and the name of a 1-D record-array into which to place the file records.

macros.name: setvalue
macros.doc: The command \setvalue is used to place content into an existing array cell.

macros.name: typesetarray
macros.doc: The \typesetarray command allows for versatile ways to format your array output, including by way of tabular environments.
